_comment: Gold labels for eval/test-document.md. 'evidence' = verbatim span(s) that must appear in a retrieved chunk for it to count as the right chunk (survives re-chunking). 'keyFacts' = strings (or arrays of accepted alternatives) the answer must contain; omit for yes/no and abstention questions, which are judged by the LLM grader. category: factual | numeric | paraphrase | distractor | multi-chunk | negative | unanswerable.

questions.question: Which custom exception does the lab library define, and is it checked or unchecked?
questions.expected: LabException, which is unchecked.
evidence: The lab library defines one custom exception, LabException, and it is unchecked.

questions.question: How is the standard library's PriorityQueue implemented, and what do offer and poll cost?
questions.expected: It is a binary min-heap; offer and poll take O(log n) time.
evidence: A PriorityQueue in the standard library is a binary min-heap, so offer and poll take O(log n) time while peek takes O(1).

questions.question: Which algorithm does the course use for shortest paths in graphs with negative edge weights?
questions.expected: Bellman-Ford.
evidence: so the course uses Bellman-Ford for those graphs

questions.question: What stack-size flag do the lab scripts pass to the JVM, and how big is each thread's stack?
questions.expected: The flag is -Xss512k, giving each thread a 512 KB stack.
evidence: The lab scripts start every program with the flag -Xss512k, which gives each thread a stack of 512 KB.

questions.question: How many buckets does LabHashMap start with, and at what load factor does it resize?
questions.expected: It starts with 32 buckets and doubles when the load factor passes 0.6.
evidence: The lab's LabHashMap uses separate chaining and starts with 32 buckets. It resizes by doubling the bucket array when the load factor passes 0.6

questions.question: Below what sub-array size does the lab's merge sort switch to insertion sort?
questions.expected: When a sub-array has fewer than 16 elements.
evidence: The lab's own merge sort switches to insertion sort when a sub-array has fewer than 16 elements.

questions.question: How many threads are in the fixed thread pool used by the lab assignments?
questions.expected: Exactly 4 threads.
evidence: The lab assignments use a fixed thread pool of exactly 4 threads

questions.question: How do I find the descendants of an entry in the student-written priority structure's backing storage?
questions.expected: The left child is at index 2i and the right child at 2i + 1 (the array starts at index 1).
evidence: the left child is at 2i, the right child at 2i + 1, and the parent at i / 2

questions.question: Why shouldn't the average of the lower and upper bounds be computed by adding them first?
questions.expected: Because adding two large ints can overflow.
evidence: because the sum of two large ints can overflow

questions.question: How deep can recursion go in student programs before it has to be turned into iteration?
questions.expected: More than 10,000 calls deep must be rewritten as a loop, or the grader reports a StackOverflowError.
evidence: a recursive method that goes deeper than 10,000 calls must be rewritten as a loop, or the grader will report a StackOverflowError

questions.question: What stops sorted insertions from turning the lab's search tree into a chain?
questions.expected: LabAvl keeps every node's balance factor between -1 and 1, fixing violations with rotations.
evidence: The lab's LabAvl tree prevents this by keeping the balance factor of every node between -1 and 1

questions.question: Why is the shortest-route method built on a min-priority structure unreliable when links have negative costs?
questions.expected: It gives wrong answers when an edge has a negative weight.
evidence: it gives wrong answers when an edge has a negative weight

questions.question: By what factor does LabList grow its array when it fills up?
questions.expected: It doubles the array each time (the older 1.5x value is obsolete).
evidence: it starts with an initial capacity of 8 and doubles its array each time it fills

questions.question: How many threads did the lab thread pool have in handbook version 2.4?
questions.expected: 8 threads.
evidence: and the thread pool had 8 threads

questions.question: What stack-size flag do lab programs use now, and what did handbook version 2.4 use?
questions.expected: Now -Xss512k; version 2.4 used -Xss1m.
evidence: The lab scripts start every program with the flag -Xss512k

questions.question: How many marks are lost for the overflow-prone midpoint, and how many for overriding equals without hashCode?
questions.expected: 3 marks for the overflow-prone midpoint and 5 marks for equals without hashCode.
evidence: Students lose 3 marks if they use the overflow-prone form.
it costs 5 marks on every assignment where it appears

questions.question: Can students use the old java.util.Stack class in lab code?
questions.expected: No. It is banned because it is synchronized and slow; use ArrayDeque instead.
evidence: the old Stack class is banned because it is synchronized and slow

questions.question: Which garbage collector do the lab scripts select?
questions.expected: The handbook does not say. A correct answer states that the provided material does not contain this information and does not invent one.

questions.question: How many marks is the CS-210 final project worth?
questions.expected: The handbook does not say. A correct answer states that the provided material does not contain this information and does not invent one.

questions.question: Which IDE does the course require students to use?
questions.expected: The handbook does not say. A correct answer states that the provided material does not contain this information and does not invent one.
